question: Can a cross-validation-tuned, class-balanced LightGBM classifier choose a better per-instance local-search parameter setting than a standard MLP configuration predictor on generated knapsack instances, judged by the same held-out solution quality?
method: Generated 0/1 knapsack instances (fixed seed) with per-setting local-search quality measured under a fixed evaluation budget; MLP baseline (classifier) vs CV-tuned per-setting LightGBM quality regressors choosing the highest predicted setting; test set from a shifted instance family; evaluated by mean normalised solution quality.
metric_name: mean normalised solution quality (value / optimum) on held-out test instances
baseline: Standard MLPClassifier (64-32 hidden, scaled features) predicting the local-search setting
improved: Per-setting LightGBM quality regressors (3-fold CV-tuned on training quality, seed-averaged models) on the same features; choose the setting with highest predicted quality
notes: Labels are noisy (single small grid, budget-limited search). The improved model uses the full per-setting quality information from training rather than only the argmax label, so it is not tied to label noise. Test family is shifted in size and correlation, so tree models cannot extrapolate in size. Test set used once for both models; tuning used only training CV. Results depend on the generator and budget and are not a replication of OPTICAT's deep RL results.
